title: Compositing with layers on a phone
description: Build a composition, refine the masks and keep the elements for later changes.

blocks.text: Compositing on a phone is needed where several images have to be joined and details cut out precisely. Losing the layers tool breaks the whole process, even if editing a single image still works.

quote.text: “Combine Photos” is arguably the most useful feature on this app, as it allows you to use a cutting tool while adding multiple layers. I’m a freelance artist, and this feature is absolutely crucial to my job. I don’t appreciate when Adobe randomly decides to pull features with no prior warning. Now I can’t work.

blocks.text: Carrying the edit through to a result

The person adds images as separate layers, refines the masks and changes their order. An edit to one layer can be undone, and the project saved to continue later. In the finished file the layers are merged only in the export you choose.
Where the idea has an advantage

To begin with, it is worth carrying one difficult composition through to the end on a small screen. Copying the capabilities of a desktop studio would produce an overloaded interface; the advantage has to lie in how convenient specific mobile operations are.
